name: Lipomyelomeningocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Lipomyelomeningocele

criteria.description: Presence of a subcutaneous lipomatous mass contiguous with the spinal cord
Evidence of spinal cord tethering or low-lying conus medullaris on imaging
Defect in the posterior elements of the vertebrae with herniation of neural tissue and meninges
Presence of neurological deficits such as lower limb weakness or bladder dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: presence of lipomatous mass contiguous with spinal cord, spinal cord tethering or low-lying conus on imaging, and neural tube defect with herniation of neural tissue and meninges.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by MRI imaging findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Subcutaneous lipomatous mass over the lumbosacral region
searchTerms: fatty lump under skin over lower back
soft tissue mass near lower spine

pathognomonic.symptomName: Tethered spinal cord with low-lying conus medullaris
searchTerms: spinal cord tethered low in spine
low-lying spinal cord with tight attachment

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neural tube defect with herniation of meninges and neural tissue
searchTerms: spinal defect with meninges and nerve tissue herniation
neural tube defect with sac-like protrusion

common.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata such as hairy patch or skin dimpling over lesion
searchTerms: skin signs like hairy patch or dimples over lesion
cutaneous markers such as skin tuft or pits

occasional.symptomName: Orthopedic deformities including foot deformities (e.g., clubfoot)

searchTerms: sensory loss in feet and legs

occasional.symptomName: Urinary tract infections secondary to neurogenic bladder
searchTerms: urinary infections from bladder nerve problems
increased muscle tone in lower limbs
skin hemangiomas close to affected area
vascular skin spots near lesion site

imaging: MRI showing lipomatous mass contiguous with spinal cord
MRI evidence of tethered cord and low-lying conus medullaris
CT or X-ray showing vertebral posterior element defects
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; considered a neural tube defect with multifactorial etiology
other: Physical examination revealing subcutaneous lipoma and cutaneous stigmata

distinguishingFeatures: More severe neurological deficits at birth
Open neural tube defect without overlying skin
Lipoma without associated neural tube defect or herniation

redFlags: Progressive lower limb weakness or paralysis
Loss of bladder or bowel control
Rapidly increasing size of subcutaneous mass or new neurological symptoms
references: Kothbauer KF. Spinal lipomas and lipomyelomeningoceles. Neurosurg Focus. 2007;23(2):E10.
Talamonti G, et al. Lipomyelomeningocele: clinical features and surgical treatment. Childs Nerv Syst. 2007;23(8-9):897-904.
